message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The business is fundamentally healthy: revenue grew 2% to **$391,035M**, gross margin expanded 210 bps to 46.2% (Services revenue +13% to $96,169M at 73.9% margin), **operating income** rose to **$123,216M**, and **operating cash flow** was **$118,254M** against $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. FY2024 **net income of $93,736M** and **diluted EPS of $6.08** were dampened by a one-time, non-operating $10.2B net tax charge from the EU State Aid Decision, so underlying earnings power is actually stronger than the headline decline; the only genuine soft spot was Greater China (-8%), offset by Americas/Europe Services growth and aggressive capital return ($95.0B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends). With the quote at $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72), I placed one buy limit order for **44 shares at $223.00**, which filled at $223.00 for a total of **$9,812** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily cap, priced within ~0.13% of the market, and funded from the account's existing $50,000 cash with no money moved out. I relied on the SEC-verified figures for revenue, operating income, net income, diluted EPS and operating cash flow above (note that the lookup confirmed $93,736M net income, matching the cash-flow statement and the $6.08 EPS math rather than the $103,736M misprint in the statements-of-operations table).
message.reasoning: Order filled at $223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Total today $9,812 < $20,000. Now summary paragraph.
